In [[mathematics]], the '''[[Lefschetz]] [[zeta function|zeta-function]]''' is a tool used in topological periodic and [[fixed point (mathematics)|fixed point]] theory, and [[dynamical systems]]. Given a [[continuous map]] <math>f\colon X\to X</math>, the zeta-function is defined as the formal series

:<math>\zeta_f(t) = \exp \left( \sum_{n=1}^\infty L(f^n) \frac{t^n}{n} \right), </math>

where <math>L(f^n)</math> is the [[Lefschetz number]] of the <math>n</math>-th [[iterated function|iterate]] of <math>f</math>. This zeta-function is of note in topological periodic point theory because it is a single invariant containing information about all iterates of <math>f</math>.

==Examples==
The identity map on <math>X</math> has Lefschetz zeta function

:<math> \frac{1}{(1-t)^{\chi(X)}},</math>

where <math>\chi(X)</math> is the [[Euler characteristic]] of <math>X</math>, i.e., the Lefschetz number of the identity map.

For a less trivial example, let <math>X = S^1</math> be the [[unit circle]], and let <math>f\colon S^1\to S^1</math> be reflection in the ''x''-axis, that is, <math>f(\theta) = -\theta</math>. Then <math>f</math> has Lefschetz number 2, while <math>f^2</math> is the identity map, which has Lefschetz number 0. Likewise, all odd iterates have Lefschetz number 2, while all even iterates have Lefschetz number 0. Therefore, the zeta function of <math>f</math> is

:<math>\begin{align}
\zeta_f(t) & = \exp \left( \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{2t^{2n+1}}{2n+1} \right) \\
&=\exp \left( \left\{2\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{t^n}{n}\right\} -\left \{2 \sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{t^{2n}}{2n}\right\} \right) \\
&=\exp \left(-2\log(1-t)+\log(1-t^2)\right)\\
&=\frac{1-t^2}{(1-t)^2} \\
&=\frac{1+t}{1-t}
\end{align}</math>

== Formula ==
If ''f'' is a continuous map on a compact manifold ''X'' of dimension ''n'' (or more generally any compact polyhedron), the zeta function is given by the formula

:<math>\zeta_f(t)=\prod_{i=0}^{n}\det(1-t f_\ast|H_i(X,\mathbf{Q}))^{(-1)^{i+1}}.</math>

Thus it is a rational function. The polynomials occurring in the numerator and denominator are essentially the characteristic polynomials of the map induced by ''f'' on the various homology spaces.

==Connections ==
This generating function is essentially an [[algebra]]ic form of the [[Artin–Mazur zeta function]], which gives [[geometry|geometric]] information about the fixed and periodic points of ''f''.
